KEY MESSAGE 1...Chances for soaking downpours and severe 
weather return Tuesday evening through early Wednesday morning.

As the dominate high pressure system pushes offshore, a low 
pressure system pushes east through Ontario and the trailing 
fronts sweep through New England Tuesday into Wednesday. A near 
60kt LLJ develops Tuesday into Wednesday, ushering in dewpoints 
near or slightly above 70F and high PWATs on the order of 
2.0"-2.25" across much of southern New England.

As the frontal system approaches Tuesday, showers and 
thunderstorms will begin to form primarily later in the 
afternoon/evening hours. While the greatest risk for severe 
thunderstorms continues to be to our west, a surge of SBCAPE 
1200-1500 J/kg combined with increasing K-indices and 0-3km 
helicity values will support some risk for straight-line winds 
within any thunderstorms that do form. Can't rule out a few 
brief spin-ups, but the risk remains on the lower side.

The main concern continues to be torrential rainfall given how 
water- loaded these storms could be, especially along the South 
Coast, Cape, and Islands. While model soundings indicate mid-
level winds around 30-40kts, some training of showers and 
thunderstorms cannot be ruled out. The latest ensemble guidance 
has nudged up the 24 hour QPF probs of 1"+ to near 80% along the
South Coast, with 2"+ probs remaining near 40-50% (especially 
along the Cape and Islands). Latest Flash Flood and experimental
Urban Rain Rate guidances are showing increasing probabilities 
that Providence and surrounding urban areas could approach the 
10-year ARI early Wednesday morning... near 2.3" in 2 hours or 
2.75" in 3 hours. After working with neighboring offices, 
highest confidence in heavier rain bands setting up remains over
the Mid-Atlantic/NYC locations, prompting a Flood Watch for 
those areas; however, later shifts may need to expand that Flood
Watch further up the I-95 corridor.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Limited risk for severe weather Wednesday.

Rain continues into Wednesday, with the higher chances and 
totals towards the Cape and Islands Wednesday morning into the 
afternoon. Ensembles continue to have higher probabilities for 
1"+ totals towards the Cape and Islands and along the south 
coast heading into Wednesday afternoon and evening, with low 
probs of 2"+ over the same areas though with more discrepancies 
among the guidance.

The main thing to keep an eye on will be a limited severe 
weather risk over southern New England Wednesday given the 
frontal passage. Guidance shows the cold front not pushing 
offshore until Thursday morning. By 00z Thursday, the front may 
be draped over the I-95 corridor. If anything, this would aid in
an increased severe risk for the interior. Global guidance 
indicates the midlevels drying out relatively quickly behind the
front while the latest NAM is slower to clear that moisture 
out. Something to monitor will be how much instability can be 
developed behind the front. NAM guidance has around 2100 J/kg of
MLCAPE over much of the interior Wednesday afternoon and 
evening (other guidance has values around 1500-2000 J/kg as 
well), and dewpoints increase to the low 70s. Given these 
conditions, there could be a risk for severe thunderstorms for 
Wednesday afternoon. Will continue to monitor this risk in 
coming updates.

KEY MESSAGE 3...Drying out Thursday into the latter part of the
week with seasonable temperatures and lower humidity into the 
weekend.

The cold front exits the region by Thursday morning, leaving 
drier and seasonable conditions in its wake. With the front, the
upper level trough centered over Quebec also moves off to the 
northeast. High pressure starts to build in over southern New 
England from the Great Lakes, continuing the drier conditions 
into the weekend. Temperatures aloft fall slightly, with 925 mb 
temperatures falling to around 16C for much of the second half 
of the week. Notably, Wednesday night will likely be cooler as 
925 mb temperatures may fall to as low as 10C over the interior.
Lows there could get into the low 50s. 850 mb temperatures are 
expected to mostly be around 10C as well through the back half 
of the week. Even with these reduced temperatures, the continued
high sun angle will keep temperatures from falling too low, 
keeping them seasonable. Conditions remain dry and seasonable 
until around Sunday when the flow shifts more S again, 
increasing humidity. A surface low may also pass just offshore, 
but any impacts from it -- if any at all -- are not certain at 
this time.
